issues.description: The problem statement requires Bookstore to have an initializer with signature init(books: [Book]) and a let property books. The solution implementation instead provides init() (no parameters) and assigns self.books = books (using an undefined identifier). This both mismatches the specified constructor signature and causes a compile error.
issues.suggestedFix: Modify the Bookstore initializer to match the specification: implement init(books: [Book]) and inside it assign self.books = books. Ensure the books property remains a let constant and the parameter name matches (books).

issues.description: The problem statement requires a Bookstore initializer with the signature `init(books: [Book])` (problem_statement.md lines 9-12). The solution implementation defines `init()` with no parameters and assigns `self.books = books` inside it, which is inconsistent with the required initializer signature and uses an undefined identifier. This mismatch between the required initializer name/signature and the solution implementation will confuse students mapping the requirement to code and prevents a clear, direct implementation of the specified API.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the Bookstore initializer in Sources/BookstoreLib/Bookstore.swift to match the problem specification: `init(books: [Book]) { self.books = books }`. Ensure the template and any examples expect the same initializer signature so students can directly implement the required API.
